text.p: The United States on Monday welcomed a new political accord between Russia and Ukraine as a move toward easing years of tension between the two Slavic neighbours.

The State Department said it hoped a treaty of friendship and cooperation signed on Saturday in Kiev "signals a further step toward good normal relations between the independent democratic nations of Ukraine and Russia."

"It is in the U.S. interest that these two countries develop relations of friendship and cooperation as sovereign equal members of the European and Euro-Atlantic community," spokesman John Dinger told reporters.
"We welcome the fact that with this treaty each side reaffirms its commitment to respect each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity."

The long-delayed accord signed by Presidents Boris Yeltsin of Russia and Leonid Kuchma of Ukraine ends a virtual cold war between the two former Soviet republics and commits them to a "strategic partnership."
The accord followed a deal last Wednesday over the shareout of the Black Sea fleet, which has kept the two countries at odds since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
Russia will lease Ukraine's Crimean port of Sevastopol to base its share of the fleet there for 20 years, and in return will write off part of Ukraine's huge energy debt.
